title: Obesity, morbid obesity and BMI
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's weight diagnosis and BMI, if reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for weight management.

HPI
The patient is an 81-year-old male who presents today for a follow-up evaluation regarding his weight. He reports that he has struggled to maintain a healthy weight despite previous attempts at lifestyle modifications. He currently feels limited in his mobility due to his size and expresses a desire to reduce his weight to improve his overall health. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and admits to a high-calorie diet.

Medication List
Multivitamin, Lisinopril 10mg daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. He appears in no acute distress. Physical exam reveals a BMI of 52.2. He is able to ambulate with a steady gait but reports shortness of breath with exertion.

Assessment
The patient has morbid obesity. This condition contributes to his limited mobility and increased risk for secondary complications.

Plan
We discussed a comprehensive plan to address his morbid obesity. The patient was advised to start a low-calorie, nutrient-dense diet and increase his daily physical activity through light walking. I provided a referral to a formal weight management program for supervised nutrition counseling. He will return in one month to monitor progress.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Morbid (severe) obesity documented by the provider: E66.01 (HCC 48).
BMI 52.x with a provider weight diagnosis: add Z68.43 (BMI 40 or more maps to HCC 48 on its own).

distractors.why: The provider documents morbid obesity: E66.01, not E66.9.
The BMI is documented and the provider diagnosed the weight condition: add the Z68 code.
